clue.text: Violent crime a month at the border

parts.note: May is a month of the year
a hem is the folded border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A violent offence committed in one particular month on a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is the legal name for violently maiming someone, and more loosely any violent disorder.

clue.text: Leaves a tie to crippled son

parts.note: a band ties things together

indicators.note: crippled means damaged out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone goes off leaving a tie to a disabled son.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone in the lurch is to desert them.

clue.text: Anne is not without access to her cottage

parts.note: hath, the old form of has, means possesses, that is, is not without
a way in gives access

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's wife has a means of getting to her famous cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Hathaway's Cottage at Shottery, near Stratford-upon-Avon, is a famous tourist site; read the clue as 'Anne' = '(she) hath a way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne is the first name of Shakespeare's wife, so the surname completes her name.

clue.text: Indulge in impropriety with many auxiliary verb forms

parts.note: M, the Roman thousand, stands for many
is, be and have are all forms used as auxiliary verbs
be is the base form of an auxiliary verb
have is an auxiliary verb, as in have gone

explanation.surface: Misbehaving grammatically by using lots of helping verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To act badly or behave improperly.

clue.text: Stupid clique ? Slight contradiction

parts.note: thick is an informal word for stupid
a set is a social clique

explanation.surface: Calling a clique stupid is only a mild contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight contradiction' reads as a comment on the clue, but it defines a word that contradicts 'slight' in build.
explanation.definitionFit: A stocky, heavily built person is the opposite of a slight, slender one.

clue.text: Mechanical aids for drawing

parts.note: sounds like equipment for an artist, but drawing means hauling loads

explanation.surface: Instruments that help one sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam vehicles built to haul heavy loads along roads, pulling being drawing.

clue.text: Frank, a GBs character

parts.note: candid means frank or outspoken

explanation.surface: Frankness described as a trait typical of George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.walkthrough: GBS is George Bernard Shaw, whose 1894 play is named after its heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw wrote a play titled after its heroine, the wife of a clergyman.

clue.text: Observe sound indications of sailing guides

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for observe is to be heard, not read

parts.note: to see is to observe
marks are signs or indications

explanation.surface: Watch out for audible signals that guide sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighthouses, beacons and similar landmarks visible from the water guide navigators.

clue.text: State of the Commonwealth islands

explanation.surface: Describing an island state of the Commonwealth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Commonwealth here is the Commonwealth of Australia, of which this island group is a state.
explanation.definitionFit: The island state south of the Australian mainland is a member state of that federation, and is made up of a main island plus many smaller ones.

clue.text: Fellow-worker goes to continent for Disney show

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's usual worker, from the worker ant
Asia is the largest continent

explanation.surface: A colleague transfers to the Continent to work on a Disney production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow-worker' looks like one word for colleague; split it into F and ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the 1940 Walt Disney animated feature set to classical music.

clue.text: Records of sterling in old Indian coinage

indicators.note: the letter for sterling is placed inside the coins

parts.note: annas were old Indian coins, sixteen to the rupee
L, from the Latin libra, is the pound sterling sign

explanation.surface: Accounts of British money held in old Indian coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are year-by-year historical records.

clue.text: Jade can't be mended next door

indicators.note: something mended is put back together, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Jade ornaments that are broken beyond repair, by the neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Something next door lies beside or neighbouring the thing in question.

clue.text: A train-crash in a Balkan capital

indicators.note: a crash wrecks the train, so its letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A railway accident in an Eastern European capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is in the surface already; the crash scrambles A TRAIN to reach it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirana is the capital city of Albania, in the Balkans.

clue.text: I hear the girl swindled 'er -the snake!

indicators.note: the setter says what he hears, so the words are to be spoken and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a girl ANNA conned (swindled) 'er, said in a dropped-aitch accent

explanation.surface: A cockney tale of a girl who cheated someone, ending in a cry of alarm at a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'Anna conned 'er' quickly in a non-rhotic accent and it sounds like the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a huge South American constrictor.

clue.text: Outline of French policy with a note added

parts.note: de is French for of
a party line is its policy
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A sketch of French government policy with an extra footnote.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to trace or describe in outline.

clue.text: Grey as Pompeii at last

explanation.surface: Something grey, like the ruined Roman town in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: Pompeii finished its days buried in volcanic dust from Vesuvius.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey like the residue of a fire describes a pale complexion; and Pompeii was finally smothered in volcanic cinders.

clue.text: Natives are heretics about rating

indicators.note: the heretics go about, around, the rating

parts.note: Arians followed Arius, who denied Christ's full divinity
AB, able seaman, is a naval rating

explanation.surface: Locals who are unorthodox believers concerning a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Whisky and soda drunk at dance

parts.note: high means intoxicated
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Getting tipsy on spirits and mixers at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall drink of spirits mixed with soda water over ice.

clue.text: " Ye. pampered Jades of" (Marlowe)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing last word of a famous line from Marlowe's Tamburlaine

explanation.surface: A line from Marlowe with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Tamburlaine the conqueror drives captive kings yoked to his chariot, crying 'Holla, ye pampered jades of' a continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation's missing word is the continent the captive kings came from, completing Marlowe's line.

clue.text: Nears end, roughly, of wooded upland area

indicators.note: roughly means not precisely, so these letters are set down in a loose new order

explanation.surface: Approaching the conclusion of a forested hill region, give or take.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ardennes is a forested plateau region of Belgium, Luxembourg and France.

clue.text: He adores Johnson's work in which nothing is interspersed

indicators.note: interspersed means a further piece is scattered into the work at another point
in which says the essays hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: The Idler was a series of essays by Samuel Johnson
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An admirer of Dr Johnson's essays with gaps scattered through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' puts O inside IDLER (IDOLER), and 'interspersed' adds IS further along.
explanation.definitionFit: One who worships or venerates someone.

clue.text: Death to the old radical

explanation.surface: Death compared with a radical of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Death is the great leveller, making all equal; the Levellers were radical democrats of the English Civil War era.
explanation.definitionFit: Death reduces everyone to the same state; the 1640s Levellers campaigned for equal political rights.

clue.text: Reveal how old your are? It could sink you ! .

parts.note: to leak is to reveal secretly
your age is how old you are

explanation.surface: Giving away your age could damage you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink you' is the clue's twist: water getting in through a hole can sink a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Water escaping in through a hole could sink a vessel.

clue.text: Become boss — take executive action ?

parts.note: be is a plain word for become or exist
the head is the boss of an organisation

explanation.surface: Becoming the boss and taking decisive action as an executive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executive action' is a pun on execution, cutting off someone's head.
explanation.definitionFit: An executioner's action is to decapitate, cutting the head from a condemned person.

clue.text: Very cautiously taking first drink?

parts.note: a punning description: very cautiously is the plain sense, while the word splits as a spirit followed by the sound of early, the first drink of the day

explanation.surface: Sipping the first drink of the day with great care.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something very cautiously means doing it with great delicacy and care.

clue.text: In Burma an artist can get a hearing

indicators.note: getting a hearing means the words are spoken aloud and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: A, then RA (Royal Academician, an artist), then CAN

explanation.surface: An artist in Burma is able to be listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'In Burma' stands for a place found there, a coastal region of Myanmar.
explanation.definitionFit: Arakan, now Rakhine, is a coastal state of Myanmar, formerly Burma.

clue.text: Intimacy, but no generosity

explanation.surface: Closeness, but without any open-handedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' is an old word for stingy, so being near shows no generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeness between people is intimacy; tight-fisted meanness is the absence of generosity.

clue.text: Agents to help you with the puzzle ?

definitions.text: Agents to help you with the puzzle ?

parts.words: Agents to help you with the puzzle
parts.note: chemical agents that dissolve things, read jokingly as aids for working out a crossword

explanation.surface: Helpers who assist you with a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemicals that dissolve substances, punningly things that solve.

clue.text: Make certain result is about right

indicators.note: the result word goes about, around, the letter for right

parts.note: to ensue is to result or follow on

explanation.surface: Making sure the outcome is roughly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee something is to make it sure.
